title: Patient-Specific Polyvinyl Alcohol Phantom Fabrication with Ultrasound and X-Ray Contrast for Brain Tumor Surgery Planning
protocol: Obtain pre-operative contrast-enhanced T1-weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and volumetric computed tomography (CT) data.
Convert MRI and CT data from DICOM format to NiFTI format for processing and analysis.
Obtain intraoperative ultrasound data.
Install software to segment the patient data with.
Load the patient’s volumetric CT scan in segmentation software, open the Segment Editor module and create new segmentation named ‘Skull’.
Use the ‘Threshold’ function to highlight the skull.
Remove any unwanted segmentations from the image (e.g., skin calcifications, mandible, C1/2, styloid process, CT patient frame, and annotations).
Use the ‘Scissors’ function to manually disconnect unwanted structures when viewing the model in 3D.
Utilize the ‘Islands’ function after manual disconnection of parts using the ‘Erase’ tool.
Correct any gaps in segmentation missed during thresholding using the ‘Paint’ and ‘Draw’ functions (e.g., lamina papyracea, cortical edge of the mastoid bone, ethmoid bone).
Fill in the foramen magnum using the ‘Paint’ and ‘Draw’ functions.
Create a 5 mm protruding spike upon which the lower part of the phantom model can be secured.
Apply the ‘Smoothing’ function with a median smoothing setting of 1.0 mm (3 × 3 × 1 pixels) to minimize loss of detail.
If a complete intact skull is required for surgical simulation, proceed to step 2.2.15.
For models requiring craniotomy, complete steps 2.2.7 through 2.2.14.
Add a new segmentation and name it ‘Skull Craniotomy’.
Copy the ‘Skull’ segmentation across to ‘Skull Craniotomy’ using the ‘Copy/Move Segments’ tab.
Use the ‘Scissors’ function to remove an appropriately-sized craniotomy in ‘Skull Craniotomy’.
Add a new segmentation and name it ‘Craniotomy Only’.
Select the segmentation ‘Skull Craniotomy’ and use the ‘Logical Operator’ function to subtract ‘Skull Craniotomy’ from ‘Skull’.
Erase everything except the desired craniotomy on the correct side of the tumor in ‘Craniotomy Only’, then save.
Subtract ‘Craniotomy only’ from ‘Skull Craniotomy’ and save.
Export the ‘Skull Craniotomy’ as a stereolithography (STL) file from the ‘Segmentations’ module.
Import the STL file ‘Skull Craniotomy’ into 3D modeling software.
Complete the ‘Flip Normals’ function if the model appears in striped pink by selecting the complete model and then ‘Edit | Flip Normals’.
Reduce the number of triangles to improve computational time.
Select the complete model then ‘Edit | Reduce’ until the total number of triangles is less than 500,000.
Apply ‘Smoothing’ function ensuring the ‘Shape Preserving’ box remains ticked.
Select the complete model then ‘Deform | Smooth’.
Click ‘Analysis’ then ‘Inspector’ and use this function to detect any small defects in the model and click auto-repair (suggest ‘Flat-fill’ selection).
Cut 'Skull' to create a top and bottom using the ‘Edit/Plane’ cut function.
Select ‘Keep Both Slices’ and ‘Remeshed’ fill type.
Change skull to transparent with ‘Shaders’ function to provide a better internal view of the skull and adjust the plane so that it is parallel to the skull base.
Separate shells by selecting ‘Edit | Separate shells’ and rename ‘Skull_Top’ and ‘Skull_Bottom’ within the objects browser.
Select ‘Hide’ for one or the other shell using the eye icon in the objects browser.
Click ‘Meshmix’ then select ‘Cylinder’ to create a dowel.
Edit size of the cylinder to 4 mm × 10 mm × 4 mm using the ‘Edit | Transform’ function.
Hide ‘Skull_Bottom’ by clicking the eye icon to remove from view.
Select ‘Edit | Align’ planes.
Choose ‘Surface point’ for the ‘Source’ (left click end transparent cylinder).
For the ‘Destination’, choose ‘Surface point’ (Shift + left click undersurface of ‘Skull_Top’).
Move dowel into skull using the green arrow.
Adjust position with blue and red arrows.
Rename ‘Dowel_Anterior’.
Make 3 copies of the dowel.
Rename one copy ‘Dowel_Posterior’.
Rename another copy ‘Dowel_Left’.
Rename the last copy ‘Dowel_Right’.
Move each dowel to the desired location using the ‘Edit | Transform’ function.
Resize an additional dowel to 3 mm × 10 mm × 3 mm.
Rename the resized dowel ‘Dowel’.
Create holes for dowels in the skull using the ‘Boolean Difference’ function.
Select ‘Skull_Top’ and a dowel, then use the ‘Boolean Difference’ tab with ‘Auto-reduce’ switch off.
Repeat the Boolean operation for each dowel on ‘Skull_Top’.
Hide ‘Skull_Top’, view ‘Skull_Bottom’, repeat the Boolean difference process for each dowel on ‘Skull_Bottom’.
Export ‘Skull_Top’, ‘Skull_Bottom’, and ‘Dowel’ as separate binary STL files.
Upload contrast enhanced T1 MRI of the brain to http://niftyweb.cs.ucl.ac.uk/program.php?p=GIF.
Download the GIF parcellation output file.
Load the contrast enhanced T1 MRI into segmentation software.
Load the GIF parcellation output file into the segmentation software.
Open the ‘Segment Editor’ module and create a new segmentation.
Select appropriate labels and combine them to form a single segmentation.
Use the ‘Smoothing’ function (suggested median 2.00 mm, 5 × 5 × 3 pixels).
Use the ‘Scissors’ function to remove any unwanted or erroneous segmentations.
Save ‘Brain’ and ‘Cerebellum’ segmentations.
Open ‘Segmentations’ module and export ‘Brain’ and ‘Cerebellum’ as STL files.
Open segmentation software and load the contrast enhanced T1 MRI.
Create new segmentation named ‘Tumor’ in the ‘Segment Editor’ module.
Use the ‘Threshold’ function to highlight the tumor.
Correct the segmentation using the ‘Paint’, ‘Draw’ and ‘Erase’ functions.
Apply the ‘Smoothing’ function (suggested median 2.00 mm, 5 × 5 × 3 pixels).
Create a new segmentation named ‘Cerebellum_Tumor’.
Combine the ‘Cerebellum’ model and ‘Tumor’ using the ‘Logical Operators | Add’ function.
Save ‘Tumor’ and ‘Cerebellum_Tumor’ segmentations.
Open ‘Segmentations’ module and export ‘Tumor’ and ‘Cerebellum_Tumor’ as STL files.
Split the ‘Brain’ segmentation into two hemispheres using the ‘Plane cut’ tool.
Save each hemisphere as a separate STL file ‘Brain right’ and ‘Brain left’.
Import the STL file ‘Tumor’ into CAD software.
Use the ‘Reduce’ function to reduce the size of the tumor model.
Convert the imported mesh to a body using the ‘Mesh to BRep’ tool.
Create a box around the tumor as a new body.
Cut the tumor from the box using the ‘Combine’ tool.
Check that the hollowed-out box is present.
Cut the hollowed-out box into an appropriate number of pieces.
Create planes through the box where the mold needs to be cut.
Click ‘Construct’, then select ‘Midplane’ to create a plane through the center of the box.
Right click on the created plane and choose ‘Offset Plane’ for precise positioning.
Use the ‘Split Body’ function in the ‘Modify’ tab to split the mold along the planes created.
Move individual pieces of the mold, by right clicking and selecting ‘Move/Copy’, so that all pieces face outwards.
Create sketch, then use ‘Centre diameter circle’ to draw small circles on each face for rivets.
Right click and select ‘Extrude’ these circles outwards a few millimeters on one face.
On corresponding faces, extrude the circles inwards slightly larger (approximately 1.5 mm) than those extruded outwards.
Save each piece of the mold as a separate STL file.
Repeat steps for ‘Brain left’, ‘Brain right’, and ‘Cerebellum tumor’ molds.
Print the 3D molds.
Install or open 3D printing software.
Open the STL file for each piece of the mold in the printing software and rotate it so that it lies flat against the build plate.
Choose a large layer height (around 0.2 mm) and low infill value (around 20%) for faster printing.
Print the molds using a rigid material such as Polylactic acid (PLA).
Open the ‘Skull Top’ file in the printing software and choose a large layer height (around 0.2 mm) and low infill value (around 20%).
Select to ‘Add support’ in the software for skull model.
Print the skull model in PLA.
Submerge the printed top and bottom of the skull in water overnight to dissolve away the PVA support material.
Measure 200 g of PVA powder and set to the side.
Heat 1800 g of deionized water to 90 °C.
Add heated water to a 2L conical flask.
Suspend the conical flask in a temperature-controlled water bath set at 90 °C.
Position an electronic stirrer in the flask, ensuring it does not touch the bottom or sides, and set the speed to 1500 rpm.
Gradually add PVA powder to the conical flask over around 30 min.
Leave the mixture to stir for another 90 min.
Remove the conical flask from the water bath and pour its contents into a beaker.
Cover the top of the beaker with cling film.
Allow the gel to cool to room temperature (around 20 °C).
Add 0.5 w/w% potassium sorbate to the PVA-c as a preservative, and manually stir well.
Measure out enough PVA-c to fill the tumor mold into a beaker.
To the PVA-c for the tumor, add 1 w/w% glass microspheres for ultrasound contrast and 5 w/w% Barium Sulfate for X-ray contrast.
Stir by hand.
Sonicate the beaker to ensure homogenous mixing of the additives.
Leave the mixture to cool and allow bubbles to escape for around 10 minutes.
Pour PVA-c into a mold through the hole in the top, allowing any bubbles to escape.
Perform two freeze-thaw cycles on the tumor; each cycle consists of 6 hours freezing at -20°C followed by 6 hours thawing at room temperature.
Carefully remove the phantom from the mold after freeze-thaw cycles.
Place the tumor into the corresponding space in the cerebellum mold, then secure and construct the rest of the cerebellum mold.
Add 0.05 w/w% glass microspheres to remaining PVA-c.
Repeat steps for pouring, cooling, freezing, thawing, removing from mold, placing in cerebellum mold, securing, and constructing the phantom.
Pour the PVA-c into the cerebellum mold, allowing it to surround the tumor that has been placed inside.
Perform two freeze-thaw cycles on each brain hemisphere and the cerebellum; each cycle consists of 24 h of freezing at -20 °C followed by 24 h of thawing at room temperature.
Carefully remove phantoms from molds after they have thawed for the second time.
Place the ‘Cerebellum tumor’ phantom on the spike at the base of the ‘Skull Bottom’ model.
Place models of two brain hemispheres (‘Brain left’ and ‘Brain right’) on top and slot them into the uppermost part of the ‘Cerebellum tumor’.
Insert four dowels in each space on the ‘Skull Bottom’ model.
Place the ‘Skull Top’ model on top.
Apply ultrasound gel to the imaging probe.
Image the brain and tumor through the craniotomy, with a clinical scanner and burr hole probe.
Image the whole phantom in a CT scanner.
